Japan has broken free from the post-war regime, and China's strategy against it has completely failed.  
(kuroranger30 perspective, February 16, 2026)

[Why Japan Does Not Need Territorial Expansion]  
As an island nation, Japan has no need for continental or peripheral territorial expansion due to geopolitical reality. Relying on imported resources and food, Japan's core survival strategy is sea-lane defense and deterrence centered on the US-Japan alliance. Lessons from pre-WWII continental advances make expansion excessively costly and irrational.

[Why China Desperately Needs Expansion]  
As a continental power, China faces a blockade structure imposed by the First Island Chain, severely restricting its strategic access to the Pacific. Breaking through Taiwan, the Nansei (Southwest) Islands, and Okinawa is essential for blue-water naval deployment, resource sea-lane control, and completion of A2/AD strategy.  
Expansion is a 'mandatory requirement' for survival and hegemony pursuit.

[Why China Wants to Bind Japan to the Post-War Regime]  
If Japan escapes the defeated-nation framework—qualitatively improving defense capabilities, potentially intervening in a Taiwan contingency, and recovering national strength through proactive fiscal policy—China's First Island Chain breakthrough will be physically and psychologically blocked.  
Using the framework of new unrestricted warfare—historical cards, propaganda, and diplomatic intimidation—China seeks to implant self-restraint in Japan: 'You must obey the authority of the United Nations.'  
This is China's core containment strategy.

[Why China Cannot Let Go of the United Nations]  
By maintaining its permanent UN Security Council veto power, China fixes the post-war order to its advantage. It blocks Japan's bid for permanent membership or order evolution, using the UN as a psychological warfare and diplomatic tool.  
References to Japan as an 'old enemy state'—ignoring the obsolescence of the relevant clauses—are part of preserving this superiority.

[How All These Elements Connect]  
The fundamental asymmetry: China's expansion is mandatory, Japan's defense is sufficient.  
China seeks to lock Japan into the image of 'aggressor / defeated nation,' using the UN (Security Council veto) as a shield to preserve the post-war regime. By repeating unreasonable demands, it attempts to psychologically paralyze Japan and remove obstacles to Pacific access.

'Japan Has Already Escaped the Post-War Regime, and China's Strategy Has Failed'  
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's landslide Lower House election victory (LDP 316 seats) secured a national mandate for 'responsible proactive fiscal policy,' 'strong economy and defense.'

'Davos 2026': Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama declared in English 'the era of cutting is over,' internationally highlighting strategic investment in AI and semiconductors (public support exceeding $66 billion, inducing over $330 billion in public-private scale).  
This shattered the 'inward-looking defeated nation' image and clearly demonstrated proactive economic security posture.

'Munich Security Conference 2026': Foreign Minister Wang Yi named and criticized PM Takaichi's Taiwan contingency remarks as 'the ghost of militarism.'  
However, Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi immediately rebutted 'no basis in fact,' Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi emphasized 'rule of law, freedom of navigation, respect for sovereignty,' and explained deepening US-Japan alliance and multi-layered Indo-Pacific partnerships.  
The Foreign Ministry lodged a stern protest over 'lack of grounds.'  
China's propaganda backfired amid European realism (defense spending increases and China vigilance).

[Not Failure—But Japan Becoming the Center of First Island Chain Reinforcement]  
China's psychological warfare and verbal attacks completely backfired.  
The Trump administration's National Defense Strategy (NDS) explicitly designates the 'Nansei Islands–Taiwan–Philippines' First Island Chain for robust defense buildup, positioning Japan, Taiwan, and the Philippines as central deterrence hubs.  
Under the Takaichi administration, revision of the three security documents advanced ahead of schedule (within 2026), defense budget acceleration, Nansei Islands fortification (Yonaguni mid-range missile deployment, radar/ammo depot buildup), and Pacific front defense strengthening (including Ogasawara) are progressing.  
China's military buildup and Taiwan intimidation instead strengthened US-Japan alliance cohesion, propelling Japan to the key position of 'deterrence by denial' on the First Island Chain.  
Result: China's Pacific access is obstructed, First Island Chain breakthrough becomes far more difficult.  
Verbal attacks, far from paralyzing Japan, summoned national mandate and international realism, sealing China's strategic failure.

[Next Step: Review of the UN and Useless International Organizations]  
Permanent UNSC membership is impossible due to China's veto.  
Limit engagement with the UN core to minimum, and distance from useless parts (Human Rights Council, climate frameworks, etc.) by 'letting unreasonable demands pass.'  
With the Trump administration's withdrawal from 66 organizations and funding halt, multilateralism is collapsing.  
Japan too will review contributions, demand reforms, and shift to effective alternative frameworks (FOIP, QUAD, US-Japan-Australia-India, European partnerships).  
Neutralizing China's UN tool usage.

Everything connects perfectly without forcing it  
China's strategy of 'keeping Japan locked as the villain' collapsed through Takaichi-Katayama's Davos response and resolute rebuttal at Munich.  
The psychological shackles of the post-war regime have been shed.  
As a result, the First Island Chain is reinforced with Japan at the center, and Asian nations now desire a strong Japan. In the kuroranger30 framework of Donroe Doctrine (inward self-reliance + alliance strengthening) vs China's new unrestricted warfare, this is the decisive historical turning point.

And surrounding countries now desire a strong Japan.  
This is the culmination of 80 years of Japan adhering to international rules  
Asian nations (excluding China), facing China's maritime expansion, economic coercion, and gray-zone actions, actively desire a 'strong Japan' as a regional stability counterbalance.  
The Philippines and Vietnam welcome Japan's defense equipment provision and joint exercises in the South China Sea.  
Indonesia and Malaysia position Japan as a trusted partner in economic security and supply-chain diversification.  
Over 80 postwar years, Japan built trust through constitutional compliance, ODA economic support, and rule-of-law diplomacy. China's propaganda (revival of militarism) no longer works due to this accumulation. As China's threats materialize, Asian middle powers evaluate Japan as 'guardian of rule-based order,' and voices desiring a strong Japan grow louder.

This is precisely the 'culmination' of postwar Japan's international trust, and the paradoxical outcome where China's containment strategy isolates itself.

Japan needs no expansion—just sufficient defense suffices; China's expansion is blocked, and reliance on the UN is shed.  
With this, China's strategy has completely failed.
